item.title: Too much RNA can starve cells of energy, scientists discover
item.description: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected danger lurking inside cells: too much RNA can damage the structures responsible for producing energy. A new study found that excess RNA, including the normally essential messenger RNA (mRNA), can directly disrupt mitochondria without relying on the immune system. The discovery could help explain how viral infections and certain aging-related diseases damage cells. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: The oxygen in about every other breath we take comes from microscopic cells—phytoplankton—drifting in the surface of the ocean. It single-handedly accounts for roughly 10% of all the carbon that the land and the oceans pull from the atmosphere each year. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Visual artist Amadeo Carvalho explores Black identity
item.description: From Cape Verde to London and beyond, Amadeo Carvalho is a self-taught, London-based contemporary visual artist putting Black identity, memory and heritage at the heart of his work. Blending painting, poetry and photography, his art explores the stories, silences and connections that shape who we are. This weekend, his powerful collection "Portraits of Absence" arrives at the AKAA Art Fair here in Paris, where it will be exhibited by the curatorial platform Casa Vicência.
